ordered_diagnoses: Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) with Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS)

s1.syndrome_frame: Acute respiratory illness with fever and hypoxia
salient_findings: Fever up to 39°C
Anosmia
Shortness of breath
Oxygen saturation of 85% on room air
Coarse rales at the lung bases bilaterally
Bilateral multifocal pneumonia on chest radiography
key_facts: Oxygen saturation of 85% on room air
Coarse rales at the lung bases bilaterally
Nasopharyngeal swab positive by reverse transcriptase–polymerase chain reaction
Chest radiography suggestive of bilateral multifocal pneumonia
Normal sinus rhythm with normal frontal QRS axis on ECG

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including fever, anosmia, and shortness of breath, combined with a nasopharyngeal swab positive by reverse transcriptase–polymerase chain reaction and chest radiography suggestive of bilateral multifocal pneumonia, are consistent with COVID-19 pneumonia.

rejected.label: Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) with Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS)
rejected.why: While the patient has severe respiratory symptoms, the information provided does not specifically indicate the full criteria for ARDS, such as a known pulmonary or extrapulmonary cause of the acute respiratory failure and a ratio of partial pressure of arterial oxygen to fraction of inspired oxygen below a certain threshold.

rejected.label: Influenza pneumonia
rejected.why: The positive nasopharyngeal swab by reverse transcriptase–polymerase chain reaction specifically points towards COVID-19 rather than influenza.

rejected.label: Pneumococcal pneumonia
rejected.why: There is no specific indication of pneumococcal infection, such as a positive blood culture or a specific response to pneumococcal antigens.

rejected.label: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS)
rejected.why: ARDS is a condition that can result from various causes, including COVID-19 pneumonia, but the diagnosis of ARDS alone does not account for the specific viral etiology indicated by the positive nasopharyngeal swab.
